title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is navigating a complex landscape where geopolitical tensions and regulatory frameworks are reshaping competitiveness. Meanwhile, funding continues to flow into innovative ventures, signaling a cautious optimism amid the challenges.

themes.title: Regulatory Concerns in Europe
themes.body: The EU Space Act is raising alarms among European space firms, who fear it could hinder their competitive edge in a rapidly evolving market. As the industry grapples with these regulations, the emphasis on agility becomes even more critical.

themes.title: Geopolitical Shifts Open Opportunities
themes.body: As global tensions rise, companies like SpinLaunch are finding new avenues for growth, capitalizing on the shifting dynamics of space access. This could lead to innovative solutions that challenge traditional launch methods.

themes.title: Funding Flows into Space Ventures
themes.body: Recent investments, including True Anomaly's $190M Series C, highlight a growing confidence in the space sector's potential. With the Defense-Tech IPO window showing signs of life, expect more startups to vie for a piece of the action.

themes.title: Military and Commercial Collaborations
themes.body: The partnership between Anduril and L3Harris on a tactical SDA constellation bid underscores the increasing overlap between military needs and commercial capabilities. This trend could redefine how defense and space industries collaborate in the future.
